claims.text: Throat culture is the most reliable way to tell viral pharyngitis from group A strep.
claims.quote: In tonsillopharyngitis, throat culture is the most reliable way to differentiate viral infection from GABHS.

claims.text: Children: rapid strep test in the office; treat if positive, send a culture if negative.
claims.quote: one strategy in children is to do a rapid strep screen (rapid antigen detection test) in the office and treat empirically if positive, and if negative, send a formal culture to a laboratory for testing.

claims.text: Adults meeting clinical criteria (tonsillar exudate, tender nodes, fever, no cough): throat culture for all bacterial pathogens.
claims.quote: In adults, because other bacterial pathogens may be involved, throat culture for all bacterial pathogens is appropriate for those meeting clinical criteria described previously (tonsillar exudate, tender lymphadenomegaly, fever or history of fever, absence of cough).

claims.text: Mononucleosis, gonorrhea or HIV testing only when clinically suspected.
claims.quote: Testing for mononucleosis, gonorrhea, or HIV infection is done only when clinically suspected.

claims.text: Neck CT right away if an abscess's location and extent are unclear.
claims.quote: Many abscesses are managed clinically, but if location and extent are unclear, immediate CT of the neck should be done.

claims.text: Possible epiglottitis: a lateral neck x-ray only if the patient doesn't look seriously ill and has no respiratory symptoms.
claims.quote: Patients who do not appear seriously ill and have no respiratory symptoms may have lateral neck radiographs to look for edematous epiglottis.
